Team

 


Research and Context

  • Goal: Generate additional revenue through sales options in the profile section
  • Foundation: Moving subscription information up to the profile level can give more visibility to subscription plans, making it easier for users to view and access available options. This change may also simplify navigation and reduce the steps needed for users interested in upgrading or renewing their subscription, ultimately boosting conversion rates

Research results

Right now, the profile consists of two nested levels:

  • Profile
  • Settings

Currently, subscription information is hidden within the settings, so it’s not visible upon opening the profile. In this experiment, we’ll try moving the information about plans directly into the profile to make it visible to a larger audience.

— we also previously conducted an experiment with an offboarding process, where we tested moving subscription plans into the profile for a limited audience. This change resulted in an additional X (tbd ) accesses per day.

Description of the Solution & Mockups

Iteration 1

Solution

  • For all types of subscriptions, we will move the plans to the personal account

  • If there is access to the subscription, we will highlight the corresponding plan

  • Purchased subscriptions cannot be edited or canceled

  • We create a profile layout that accommodates both registered and unregistered users

    • In both cases, we will move the profile settings to a separate section, which can be accessed by clicking on the gear icon

Description of the Solution & Mockups

Solution

Instead of selling single plans, offer bundles, and upgrade purchased single plans to a unified subscription

  • We’re preparing an experiment for an audience that doesn’t have any access

  • In the profile, in the subscriptions section, display a banner for purchasing the unified subscription Pro+Courses+Sing

  • The instant bundle price of 69.99 is displayed on the banner, so clicking on the banner should lead directly to the purchase, bypassing the paywall

  • If the user is without an account and without access in the app, we should also show them the banner with the bundle offer

Plans

  • iOS: com.ultimateguitar.ugt.pro_edu_sing.instant.1year
  • Android: com.ultimateguitar.tabs.p_e_s.inst.1year

Decision

Results

  • arpu significantly increased by 37% on iOS and 34% on Android
  • we increased subscription section reach 4 times from account

Conclusion GreenSuccess

  • The new source from profile has proven highly effective, driving strong sales

  • We have a clear improvement in accesses / arpu

  • Works well for former subscribers

  • Users might respond more positively to non-marketing sources that don’t push aggressive sales toward them

  • There was a bug with pro/lifetime users who saw "Resubscribe" button in account in test variation
    • some of them purchased it again

  • Rolling out this iteration and preparing the next one

Next steps

  • Relaunch second iteration with unified offer
  • Address repeat purchases in the next iteration

trueIteration #3

#5 601 - Redfailed

Decision

Results

  • No significant changes in terms of revenue for both variations. 
  • The 3rd group (bundle) looks even worse in terms of the main metrics, the 2nd group (only Pro) in general does not differ significantly from the test group.

Conclusion 

  • Despite some minor successes on Android, the target metrics were not achieved

  • B: a little higher 1d retention (only for iOS), but not significantly (probably by chance). for those who have selected a tariff plan on the account page: a little more accesses to a Pro plan through iOS, but less to Courses and bundles (Pro + Courses + Sing). Almost no changes for Android users.
  • C: Expectedly more accesses to bundle (Pro + Courses + Sing), however conversions (trial, charges) are much lower, therefore ARPU is lower (significantly for iOS).  
  • After launching the experiment, the app’s interface and navigation changed: profile access is now at the top of the page and less noticeable. As a result, the collected data can no longer be considered fully relevant

  • Nevertheless, the profile from the first iteration has been rolled out and will remain in the same format

  • The feature comparison element can be reused in other places, such as on Explore instead of a banner

  • We won’t continue developing the experiment in this form, but we’re closing it as successful since we rolled out the first variation

Research and Context

  • Goal: Generate additional revenue through sales options in the profile section
  • Foundation: Moving subscription information up to the profile level can give more visibility to subscription plans, making it easier for users to view and access available options. This change may also simplify navigation and reduce the steps needed for users interested in upgrading or renewing their subscription, ultimately boosting conversion rates

Research results

Right now, the profile consists of two nested levels:

  • Profile
  • Settings

Currently, subscription information is hidden within the settings, so it’s not visible upon opening the profile. In this experiment, we’ll try moving the information about plans directly into the profile to make it visible to a larger audience.

[2024-07-01] UG App: offboarding — canceling a subscription within the app [2025-04-09]— we also previously conducted an experiment with an offboarding process, where we tested moving subscription plans into the profile for a limited audience. #5 601 07 Jan 2025-16 Jan 2025 FAILED

Decision

Results

  • No significant changes in terms of revenue for both variations. 
  • The 3rd group (bundle) looks even worse in terms of the main metrics, the 2nd group (only Pro) in general does not differ significantly from the test group.

Conclusion 

  • Despite some minor successes on Android, the target metrics were not achieved

  • B: a little higher 1d retention (only for iOS), but not significantly (probably by chance). for those who have selected a tariff plan on the account page: a little more accesses to a Pro plan through iOS, but less to Courses and bundles (Pro + Courses + Sing). Almost no changes for Android users.
  • C: Expectedly more accesses to bundle (Pro + Courses + Sing), however conversions (trial, charges) are much lower, therefore ARPU is lower (significantly for iOS).  
  • After launching the experiment, the app’s interface and navigation changed: profile access is now at the top of the page and less noticeable. As a result, the collected data can no longer be considered fully relevant

  • Nevertheless, the profile from the first iteration has been rolled out and will remain in the same format

  • The feature comparison element can be reused in other places, such as on Explore instead of a banner

  • We won’t continue developing the experiment in this form, but we’re closing it as successful since we rolled out the first variation
